title: Rows by position and by label
summary: iloc picks rows and columns by position (0, 1, 2 …), like counting down a list. loc picks them by label: the index value and the column names. set_index() makes a column, such as Player, the labels, so df.loc["Arjun Rao", "Runs"] reads one cell. idxmax() gives the label of the biggest value.
objectives: Pick rows and columns by position with iloc.
Make a column the index with set_index().
Read a row or one cell by label with loc.
Find who has the biggest value with idxmax().

slides.h: By the end: “Siddharth Jain’s runs” in one step
slides.say: Counting rows works for the first row or the last, but analysts think in names: “show me Siddharth Jain”. By the end you’ll look rows up by name.
points: `df.iloc[0:3, 0:2]`: the first 3 rows and first 2 columns (the end isn’t included, as with range).
p: Counting rows works for the first row or the last, but analysts think in names: “show me Siddharth Jain”. By the end you’ll look rows up by name.
`df.iloc[0:3, 0:2]`: the first 3 rows and first 2 columns (the end isn’t included, as with range).

slides.h: iloc is positions, loc is labels
slides.say: Mixing them up is the classic mistake: `p.iloc["Arjun Rao"]` stops with TypeError, and `df.loc[0:2]` **includes** label 2 (labels, unlike positions, include the end).
points: iloc: whole numbers only, end left out.
`df["Runs"].idxmax()` gives the **label** of the biggest value; with Player as the index, that’s a name.
